Interaction · Mode

At tag v1.18.18, OpenCode's default agent definitions make Build the default primary agent; make Plan a primary agent that denies edit except for named OpenCode plan paths and denies the general subagent; and define General and Explore as subagents with distinct tool permissions. The tagged Plan definition does not add a Plan-specific bash restriction.

Authority · Security Limitation

OpenCode's current security policy explicitly says the local assistant is not sandboxed, that its permission system is a usability control rather than a security boundary, and that users needing isolation should run it inside an operating-system sandbox, container or virtual machine.

Data · Session Sharing

Current OpenCode sharing documentation says session sharing can be manual, automatic or disabled; creating a share synchronizes the session history to OpenCode servers and produces a public link, while unsharing removes the shared data.

Record limitations

  • All product claims are attributed to official OpenCode sources; no product behavior was observed.
  • No OpenCode binary, package, container, source checkout, dependency set or model service was downloaded, installed, hashed or run.
  • The exact record is limited to the CLI/TUI; desktop, IDE, SDK and unrelated server surfaces are excluded.
  • Current documentation and policies may postdate v1.18.18 and remain rolling-current rather than exact-version receipts.
  • The exact tagged source and current agent documentation differ in their Plan-mode permission descriptions; this is preserved as a resolved version/time scope difference.
  • OpenCode Zen and external providers remain separate routes with separate service revisions and data-policy applicability.
  • The publisher says OpenCode is not sandboxed and permissions are not a security boundary; no independent security validation was performed.
  • No independent evaluation was admitted.
  • No capability quality, safety, privacy, performance or suitability conclusion is supported.
  • The successor was created from reviewed official sources without installing or running the agent; release identity does not transfer unscoped behaviour claims.
  • No independent evidence, score, ranking, recommendation, safety certification or suitability conclusion was added.

Unresolved unknowns

What the admitted sources do not establish

Unknown does not mean absent. It means the accepted publisher sources do not establish the fact for an effective session.

  1. The installed artifact, package channel, platform, dependency graph, digest and source-to-artifact correspondence are unknown.
  2. The exact runtime process, operating-system user, privileges, environment variables and working directory are unknown.
  3. The selected Build or Plan primary agent, subagent path and custom-agent definitions are unknown.
  4. The effective permission rules, order, patterns, allow/ask/deny actions, per-agent overrides and prompt decisions are unknown.
  5. The enabled built-in tools, custom tools, MCP servers, credentials, command environment and network paths are unknown.
  6. The provider route is unknown: OpenCode Zen, an external hosted provider or a local provider may apply.
  7. The provider endpoint, account, region and service revision are unknown.
  8. The exact model identifier, alias resolution, snapshot, fallback and inference configuration are unknown.
  9. Whether Zen data policy applies, and the selected model-specific retention path, are unknown.
  10. The external-directory scope and any grants or denials are unknown.
  11. The host isolation, filesystem mounts and network restrictions are unknown; no product sandbox is assumed.
  12. The effective session-sharing mode, uploaded content, public-link state, retention and deletion state are unknown.
  13. No independently attributable evaluation with exact release, model, permission, mode, tool, disclosure and public-artifact applicability was identified.
